items.stem: A student claims: "n + n + n = n³" Identify the error in this claim and correct it.
items.answer: Adding three n’s gives 3n; n³ means multiplying three n’s.

items.stem: With the help of a specific example, explain why 3n and n³ are different.
items.answer: 3n = n + n + n (three lots of n), while n³ = n × n × n; for n = 2, 3n = 6 but n³ = 8. (A specific, correct example that illustrates this is required for full marks.)

items.answer: (a) £38.98 (b) d = (C − 3)/2.57 (c) 11.2 km (round down so the fare does not exceed the budget)
items.markingKey: (a) £38.98 (b) d = (C − 3)/2.57 (c) 11.2 km (round down so the fare does not exceed the budget). Substitution (M1 A1); rearrangement with inverse operations (M1 A1); interpretation of the result in context (D: R1).

items.stem: Which is the correct expansion of 4(c − 3)?
items.markingKey: D. Multiply both terms by 4: 4c − 12.

items.stem: Outline the meaning of the term "term".
items.answer: A single number, variable, or product of numbers and variables, separated from other terms by + or − signs
items.markingKey: 1 mark for the core idea: a single number, variable, or product of numbers and variables, separated from other terms by + or − signs. Award full marks only if the defining feature is clear; a vague example alone scores 0.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "highest common factor (HCF)"?
options: A term with a fixed value that does not contain a variable
Write an expression as a product of factors, the reverse of expanding
The largest number or term that divides exactly into every term of an expression
Terms that contain exactly the same variables raised to the same powers, such as 3ab and −7ab
items.answer: The largest number or term that divides exactly into every term of an expression
items.markingKey: C. "highest common factor (HCF)" is the largest number or term that divides exactly into every term of an expression.

items.stem: Kenji rearranges y = 9x + 9 to make x the subject and writes x = y/9 − 9. Explain the mistake, give the correct formula and check it with y = 22.
items.answer: 9 must be subtracted before dividing by 9: x = (y − 9)/9; for y = 22, x = 13/9 (check: 9 × 13/9 + 9 = 22).
items.markingKey: Wrong order of inverse operations identified (R1); correct formula (A1); numerical check (A1).

items.stem: Explain why 3x + 4y cannot be simplified.
items.answer: 3x and 4y are unlike terms (different variables), so they cannot be collected into one term.
items.markingKey: Award marks for: 3x and 4y are unlike terms (different variables), so they cannot be collected into one term. (2 marks: one for each linked point in the chain of reasoning; no marks for assertion without explanation.)

items.stem: Mei writes: ""6 less than x" is written 6 − x." Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: "6 less than x" means start with x and subtract 6: x − 6.
items.markingKey: "6 less than x" means start with x and subtract 6: x − 6. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Elena factorises 27k + 36 as 3(9k + 12). Explain why this is not fully factorised and give the full factorisation.
items.answer: The bracket 9k + 12 still has a common factor 3; fully factorised: 9(3k + 4).
items.markingKey: Common factor remaining in the bracket identified (R1); 9(3k + 4) (A1).

items.stem: "Substituting x = −2 into x² gives −4." Explain the flaw in this statement.
items.markingKey: (−2)² = (−2)(−2) = 4. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: Lars writes: "3a + 2b = 5ab" Explain why this is inaccurate.
items.answer: 3a and 2b are unlike terms and cannot be combined; the expression stays 3a + 2b.
items.markingKey: 3a and 2b are unlike terms and cannot be combined; the expression stays 3a + 2b. 1 mark for identifying the error, 1-2 marks for the correct explanation.

items.stem: For the expression 5a² + 8ah + 6: (a) how many terms are there? (b) state the coefficient of the term containing both a and h; (c) state the constant term.
items.markingKey: Terms 5a², 8ah, 6 (A1); coefficient includes its sign: 8 (A1); constant 6 (A1).

items.stem: Use factorisation to work out 47 × 77 + 47 × 23 without a calculator.
Make l the subject of the formula P = 2l + 2w.
items.markingKey: Undo the operations in reverse order, doing the same to both sides (M1); l = (P − 2w)/2 (A1).

items.stem: Expand and simplify 3(p + 2) + 4(p + 3).
items.markingKey: Expand each bracket with signs (M1 M1); collect: 7p + 18 (A1).

items.stem: Tomás is n years old. Her brother is 18 years older and her mother is 8 times her age. Write an expression for the sum of all three ages.
items.markingKey: 10n + 18 (A1 correct operations, A1 correct order/brackets).

items.stem: Factorise fully 14a²b + 35ab.
items.markingKey: HCF of the numbers 7 (A1); common variables ab (A1); 7ab(2a + 5) (A1).

items.stem: Body mass index is BMI = m/h², with m in kg and h in metres. Find the BMI of an adult with mass 53 kg and height 1.65 m, to 1 decimal place.

An L-shaped floor plan is made of a rectangle 6x by (x + 4) and a square of side x. (a) Write and simplify an expression for the total area. (b) Write and simplify an expression for the perimeter if the square is attached along part of the side of length 6x. (c) Find the area when x = 2.
items.markingKey: (a) 7x² + 24x (b) 16x + 8 (c) 76. Expressions formed (M1); expanded and simplified correctly (M1 A1); generalisation justified algebraically (B/C: R1 C1).

items.stem: A phone plan in Mumbai costs a fixed 15 units per month plus 3 units per GB of data. (a) Write an expression for the monthly cost for g GB. (b) Isabel uses 13 GB. Find the cost. (c) Another plan costs 5g. Explain which is cheaper for small and large data use.
items.answer: (a) 15 + 3g (b) 54 (c) the second plan is cheaper when 2g < 15, i.e. g < 7.5 GB; the first is cheaper for larger use

items.stem: A rectangle has area 7x² + 21x cm². (a) Factorise the expression. (b) Mei says the rectangle could be 7x cm by (x + 3) cm or x cm by (7x + 21) cm. Explain whether both are possible. (c) Give one more pair of possible dimensions.
items.answer: (a) 7x(x + 3) (b) yes – both have product 7x² + 21x (c) e.g. 7(x + 3) cm by x cm

items.stem: A taxi in Accra charges C = 8 + 1.46d (cedis) for a journey of d km. (a) Find the cost of a 5 km journey. (b) Rearrange to make d the subject. (c) Tariq has GH₵33. How far can Tariq travel, to the nearest 0.1 km?
items.answer: (a) GH₵15.30 (b) d = (C − 8)/1.46 (c) 17.1 km (round down so the fare does not exceed the budget)
